summary: Source-anchored research for Compact integrated card production automation. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Duplo says the DC-648 camera scans barcodes and registration marks; job preparation and mark handling are part of the automation workflow. (low confidence)

The DC-ST100 brochure distinguishes automatic changeover for one to three stacks across from semi-automatic changeover for four or five. Its automation claim therefore has a layout-dependent limit. (low confidence)

The Uchida AeroCut nano operation manual warns that the machine cannot detect a double feed occurring with the first fed sheet. Double-feed detection alone therefore does not establish complete-deck integrity. (low confidence)

Equipment dealer/service provider Print & Finishing Solutions says heavy static charge can cause misfeeds, double feeds or jams on air-feed cutters. Treat this as attributed service guidance, not a measured failure rate. (low confidence)

Duplo describes the DC-648 as a single-pass slitting, cutting, creasing and perforating finisher for digitally printed sheets. This describes finishing automation, rather than evidence of a complete printed and boxed game. (low confidence)

The reviewed offerings advertise different output stages: AeroCut Nano cutting/slitting, Duplo batch stacking, and Rollem collation with downstream finishing options. Evaluate a proposed compact system against every required stage rather than treating card cutting or stacking as proof of a complete game. (medium confidence)
MBM specifies the tabletop Precision Card Pro at 18.5 by 23 by 13 inches (depth, width, height); this compactness measurement applies to its slitter/cutter. (low confidence)

Do not equate cutter speed with completed-game throughput: Duplo rates the DC-648 in sheets per minute, while MBM qualifies its card rate by letter-size paper and single-cut cards. Neither rating measures completion of the commissioned game. (medium confidence)

Duplo describes the DC-ST100 as supporting programmable batch separation and removal of completed stacks while operation continues. These features address output handling; they do not by themselves demonstrate correctly collated game decks. (low confidence)
The DC-ST100 specification restricts paper weight to 230–400 gsm and maximum stack height to 40 mm; qualify the finished stock against the stacker as well as the cutter. (low confidence)

Rollem describes the SlipStream III as able to cut, collate, punch and wrap in one pass, and says a deck can span multiple sheets. This is manufacturer evidence of integrated deck finishing, not measured performance for the commissioned game. (low confidence)

Rollem positions its AutoCollator for lower-volume or space-constrained applications, with cards presented downstream for punching, wrapping or packing. Its lower-volume positioning does not establish that every downstream operation is included in a compact unit. (low confidence)

In supplier-submitted material dated July 13, 2026, Rollem describes Cardistry as integrating slitting, cutting, collation, verification and boxing, rated up to 60 finished packs per minute. Treat the rate as a supplier claim; this article provides no independent game-specific throughput measurement. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-13)

Historical operator accounts disagree about unattended finishing: in the November 2020 PrintPlanet discussion, Wheate valued being able to perform other cutting work while a Duplo ran; SoggyWinter reported recurring feeder attention to avoid double feeds. These are model- and shop-specific anecdotes, not current reliability rates. (low confidence)

Morgana describes the AeroCut Nano as an entry-level cutting/slitting model and says its cutters can be manually adjusted for specific job sizes; the specified machine dimensions are 565(W) x632(D) x963(H) mm. This documents a compact cutter with setup work. (low confidence)

Duplo rates the DC-648 at a maximum of 40 sheets per minute and advertises slitting, cutting, creasing and perforating in one pass. This is a sheet-finishing rating, not a measured finished-deck rate. (low confidence)
Duplo’s DC-ST100 brochure, marked 0326, lists the connected DC-648/stacker dimensions as 126 by 35 by 47 inches. Floor-space planning should use the connected configuration. (low confidence)

Rollem describes the SlipStream III as trimming/slitting sheets in two directions and collating them in one pass, with die-cutting, punching and packaging offered downstream. This explicitly describes deck assembly capability beyond ordinary card cutting. (low confidence)

In its February 2018 installation announcement, operator NAPCO/Vulcan said its Rollem MK2 Slipstream could slit, trim, collate, stack, round corners, box and wrap inline. This is historical operator-reported capability, not an independent acceptance test or proof of a compact configuration. (low confidence)

MBM’s Precision Card Pro product page displays $7,244 for the slitter and cutter. This is a displayed equipment price, not a configured printer-to-boxed-game quotation; currency selection, tax, freight and installed-cost inclusions were not established. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)
